dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Gate the INFO log in `_capability_present` on `record_capability_gap(...)` returning True so log and alert share the same deduped edge, per the function's stated contract.
evidence: dispatch_apply_phases.py:190-198 `logger.info(...)` then `record_capability_gap(capability, member, site, key)` — the info call is not gated on the return
pass_io.py docstring for record_capability_gap: 'Returns True when this call wrote the record, False when it was deduped, so callers can log the INFO line on the same edge.'
dropped.finding: `record_capability_gap` returns True/False specifically so callers can gate the INFO log 'on the same edge' as the deduped alert (its docstring states this), but `_capability_present` logs the INFO line unconditionally and discards the return value. Across a batch against a non-capable backend the INFO log therefore fires once per mutation/site while the durable alert is recorded only once — the log volume contradicts the deduplication contract the return value was designed to support.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Either null out (or omit) the per-issue `key`/`local_id` on the capability-gap alert, or document that they are merely the first-seen exemplar, since the record is deduped batch-wide per (capability, site).
evidence: pass_io.py: `first = (capability, site) not in _CAPABILITY_GAPS_SEEN` then `if not first: return False` — only the first (capability,site) writes
the written record includes `"key": key` and `"local_id": local_id` bound to that first sub-op only
docstring acknowledges 'Losing the per-sub-op multiplicity costs nothing' but does not address the per-key field being misleading
dropped.finding: `record_capability_gap` dedupes per `(capability, site)` and writes the persisted `key`/`local_id` of only the FIRST skipped sub-op; every subsequent issue skipped for the same missing capability contributes no record. In a batch reconciling many issues, the single alert names an arbitrary first issue key while dozens of other issues were also skipped, so the `key`/`local_id` fields misrepresent scope.
